sentences.en: Hello and welcome to Speaking of Psychology, a podcast produced by the American Psychological
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎收听《心理学话语》，这是一档由美国心理学会制作的播客

sentences.en: Association.
sentences.zh: Association.

sentences.en: I'm your host, Audrey Hamilton.
sentences.zh: 我是主持人奥黛丽·汉密尔顿。

sentences.en: In this episode, I talk with a psychologist about why climate change scientists, communicators, and policymakers should be looking at older
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我将与一位心理学家探讨为什么气候变化科学家、传播者和政策制定者应该将老年人视为绿色思维中尚未开发的资源。

sentences.en: adults as an untapped resource for green thinking.
sentences.zh: 许多研究在气候讨论中忽视了老年人。

sentences.en: A lot of the research has overlooked older people in the climate discussion.
sentences.zh: 许多研究在气候讨论中忽视了老年人。

sentences.en: I find that
sentences.zh: 我发现

sentences.en: I'm either an aging whisperer to climate groups or a climate whisperer to aging groups because both groups are sort of like ships passing in the night.
sentences.zh: 对于气候组织来说，我像是一个懂老龄化的内部人士；对于老龄化组织来说，我像是一个懂气候的内部人士，因为这两个群体有点像夜空中交错的船只。

sentences.en: They're not talking to each other.
sentences.zh: 他们彼此没有交流。

sentences.en: In fact, psychology research has shown that older adults are primed to think about their own legacies and future generations.
sentences.zh: 事实上，心理学研究表明，老年人天生就会思考自己的遗产和子孙后代。

sentences.en: And while older adults also are more likely to vote and have time to act on climate change related issues, they are usually left feeling anxious, invisible, and undervalued.
sentences.zh: 尽管老年人更有可能投票并有时间参与气候变化相关问题，但他们通常会感到焦虑、隐形且被低估。

sentences.en: Mick Smeyer, a professor of psychology at Bucknell University, has leveraged his work in gerontology,
sentences.zh: 巴克内尔大学心理学教授米克·斯迈尔将其在老年学（即衰老研究）方面的工作，转化为针对老龄化世界开发和评估有效的气候行动策略。

sentences.en: the study of aging, into developing and evaluating effective climate action strategies for an aging world.
sentences.zh: 他的“绿色灰发”项目与气候传播者、气候科学家以及社区和商业领袖合作，使老年人在气候行动策略中更加显眼、更有价值、更有成效。

sentences.en: His Graying Green project works with climate communicators, climate scientists, and community and business leaders to make older adults more visible, valued, and effective
sentences.zh: 他的“绿色灰发”项目与气候传播者、气候科学家以及社区和商业领袖合作，使老年人在气候行动策略中更加显眼、更有价值、更有成效。

sentences.en: in climate action strategies.
sentences.zh: 在气候行动策略中。

sentences.en: Welcome, Dr. Smeyer.
sentences.zh: 欢迎您，斯迈尔博士。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: I think there's an assumption out there that younger people are more concerned about the negative repercussions of climate change.
sentences.zh: 我认为外界有一种假设，即年轻人更关心气候变化的负面影响。

sentences.en: You know, yet a recent survey done at Yale said that 45% of baby boomers are alarmed or concerned about climate change compared with just
sentences.zh: 你知道，然而耶鲁大学最近的一项调查显示，45%的婴儿潮一代对气候变化感到惊慌或担忧，相比之下，千禧一代只有

sentences.en: 35% of millennials, just as one example.
sentences.zh: 35%，这只是一个例子。

sentences.en: Does this surprise you or, you know, why or why not?
sentences.zh: 这让你感到惊讶吗？或者说，为什么会这样，为什么不会？

sentences.en: Well, that's a good question, Audrey.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是个好问题，奥黛丽。

sentences.en: It does not surprise me, but I'm biased.
sentences.zh: 这并不让我感到惊讶，但我有偏见。

sentences.en: I'm a gerontologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我是一名老年学家。

sentences.en: I've been studying aging my whole career.
sentences.zh: 我的整个职业生涯都在研究衰老。

sentences.en: So I know that older adults are thinking about the future, even if they're not going to be part of that future, even if their own time is shorter than the future they can envision.
sentences.zh: 所以我知道老年人在考虑未来，即使他们不会成为那个未来的一部分，即使他们自己的时间比他们能想象的未来还要短。

sentences.en: I also know that developmentally, older adults are primed to think about next generations in their own family.
sentences.zh: 我也知道，从发展心理学来看，老年人天生就会考虑自己家族的下一代。

sentences.en: So for those reasons, I'm not surprised that older adults are concerned about climate change and climate action in general.
sentences.zh: 因此，出于这些原因，我并不对老年人关心气候变化和总体气候行动感到惊讶。

sentences.en: And then when you get to very specific actions in their local or regional communities or that affect them or their families,
sentences.zh: 然后，当涉及到他们当地或区域社区中非常具体的行动，或者影响他们及其家人的行动时，

sentences.en: I'm not surprised that their concern is even higher.
sentences.zh: 我并不惊讶他们的担忧程度甚至更高。

sentences.en: The number of people aged 60 and older has doubled since 1980.
sentences.zh: 自1980年以来，60岁及以上的人口数量已经翻了一番。

sentences.en: The number of people aged 80 years and older will almost quadruple to 395 million between now and 2050.
sentences.zh: 从现在到2050年，80岁及以上的人口数量将几乎翻两番，达到3.95亿。

sentences.en: You have said that older populations are largely ignored resource for climate change efforts.
sentences.zh: 您曾说过，老年人口是气候变化工作中间很大程度上被忽视的资源。

sentences.en: What does the research say about older adults and the likelihood that they would become interested in environmentalism?
sentences.zh: 研究对老年人及其对环保主义产生兴趣的可能性有何见解？

sentences.en: Well, it's interesting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这很有趣。

sentences.en: A lot of the research has overlooked older people in the climate discussion.
sentences.zh: 许多研究在气候讨论中忽视了老年人。

sentences.en: I find that I'm either an aging whisperer to climate groups or a climate whisperer to aging groups because both groups are sort of like ships passing in the night.
sentences.zh: 我发现，对于气候组织来说，我像是一个懂老龄化的内部人士；对于老龄化组织来说，我像是一个懂气候的内部人士，因为这两个群体有点像夜空中交错的船只。

sentences.en: They're not talking to each other.
sentences.zh: 他们彼此没有交流。

sentences.en: So when I first started the Gray and Green
sentences.zh: 所以当我刚开始做“绿色灰发”

sentences.en: Project, I'd talk to climate scientists and I'd talk about the intersection of population aging and climate change, two global patterns, and I'd get a one-word answer.
sentences.zh: 项目时，我会和气候科学家交谈，我会谈到人口老龄化和气候变化这两个全球模式的交汇点，而我得到的回答只有一个词。

sentences.en: And that word was, huh.
sentences.zh: 那个词就是：啊？

sentences.en: And the first time I got that word, I was a little worried.
sentences.zh: 当我第一次听到这个词时，我有点担心。

sentences.en: But then I realized that, huh, is science talk for?
sentences.zh: 但后来我意识到，“啊？”是科学界的行话，意思是：

sentences.en: That's not a crazy idea.
sentences.zh: 这并不是个疯狂的想法。

sentences.en: I just never thought of it.
sentences.zh: 我只是从来没想过这一点。

sentences.en: And so we'd go on and talk, and then the climate scientists would become intrigued by, what are we missing here?
sentences.zh: 于是我们继续交谈，然后气候科学家们开始对“我们这里错过了什么”产生兴趣。

sentences.en: And I think what they're missing is that a lot of the lessons that they've developed for other age groups also apply to older people.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们所错过的是，他们为其他年龄段群体总结出的许多经验同样适用于老年人。

sentences.en: The basic lesson that comes from the National Academy of Sciences, for example, is when it comes to climate communication, keep it short, social, and positive.
sentences.zh: 例如，来自美国国家科学院的基本经验是，在进行气候传播时，要做到简短、社交化和积极。

sentences.en: Here's what that means.
sentences.zh: 这就是它的含义。

sentences.en: Short in terms of time frame.
sentences.zh: 就时间范围而言要简短。

sentences.en: We're not wired to think about our carbon footprint 10,000 years from now.
sentences.zh: 我们的天性并不习惯去思考一万年后的碳足迹。

sentences.en: In fact, we can think maybe three or four generations out.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们最多能考虑到三到四代人。

sentences.en: So short time frame really matters.
sentences.zh: 因此，短时间范围真的很重要。

sentences.en: Social, we're more likely to engage older people if we can link the climate issue to people and places that they care about, that they have a social connection to.
sentences.zh: 社交化：如果我们能将气候问题与他们关心的人和地方、与他们有社会联系的人和地方联系起来，我们就更有可能让老年人参与进来。

sentences.en: And positive, it's really important not to leave people totally overwhelmed with anxiety by how big the climate issue is.
sentences.zh: 积极性：非常重要的一点是，不要让人们完全被气候问题有多大所带来的焦虑压垮。

sentences.en: But it's important to point out the realities and also to point out what can we do about it.
sentences.zh: 但同样重要的是，要指出现实，并指出我们能做些什么。

sentences.en: What are some positive steps that individuals and communities can take?
sentences.zh: 个人和社区可以采取哪些积极的步骤？

sentences.en: So as you mentioned, you're the founder of the Gray and Green Project.
sentences.zh: 正如你所提到的，你是“绿色灰发”项目的创始人。

sentences.en: Could you tell me a bit more about the goals of that project and what you're doing to achieve those goals?
sentences.zh: 你能多跟我讲讲这个项目的目标，以及你正在采取什么行动来达成这些目标吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: Sure.

sentences.en: Gray and Green is really designed to try to move older people from anxiety to action to habit on climate change.
sentences.zh: “绿色灰发”项目的真正设计初衷，是试图推动老年人在气候变化问题上从焦虑走向行动，再走向习惯。

sentences.en: And we're doing that by engaging both climate scientists and climate communicators in this work and also developing some specific approaches and testing them out.
sentences.zh: 我们通过让气候科学家和气候传播者都参与到这项工作中来，同时开发一些具体的方法并进行测试，来实现这一点。

sentences.en: I spent the last year or so at the design school at Stanford University really trying to take design thinking and design concepts and applying it to this civic engagement issue.
sentences.zh: 过去一年左右，我在斯坦福大学设计学院度过，真正试图将设计思维和设计概念应用到这个公民参与的问题中。

sentences.en: And in that process, I spent a lot of time talking with older people about their concerns and about their feeling that they're invisible, undervalued, and ineffective
sentences.zh: 在这个过程中，我花了很多时间与老年人交流，了解他们的担忧，以及他们感觉自己在气候问题上是

sentences.en: on climate issues.
sentences.zh: 隐形的、被低估的且无能为力的感受。

sentences.en: And then working with them to figure out, well, how can we change that?
sentences.zh: 然后与他们合作，找出我们如何才能改变这种状况？

sentences.en: How can we move them from that anxiety about climate to action and then habit on climate change?
sentences.zh: 我们如何才能让他们摆脱对气候的焦虑，走向行动，进而形成气候变化的习惯？

sentences.en: And we now have a set of approaches that work.
sentences.zh: 我们现在有一套行之有效的方法。

sentences.en: And now our next step is how do we scale that from working with individuals or small groups to larger groups and communities?
sentences.zh: 我们现在的下一步是如何将这种方法从与个人或小群体的合作扩展到更大的群体和社区？

sentences.en: So what are some examples of the approaches that you're looking at?
sentences.zh: 那么，您正在研究的方法有哪些例子呢？

sentences.en: Well, let me ask you four questions, Audrey.
sentences.zh: 好吧，奥黛丽，让我问你四个问题。

sentences.en: Very simple questions.
sentences.zh: 非常简单的问题。

sentences.en: No podcast host will be harmed in the making of this recording.
sentences.zh: 在这次录音过程中，没有任何播客主持人受到伤害。

sentences.en: Picture a place, any place in the world that has a special meaning to you that you're really attached to.
sentences.zh: 想象一个地方，世界上任何对你有特殊意义、让你依恋的地方。

sentences.en: You have that place in mind?
sentences.zh: 你脑海中有那个地方了吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: Yeah.

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: Okay.

sentences.en: Picture that place affected by extreme weather or climate change.
sentences.zh: 想象那个地方受到极端天气或气候变化的影响。

sentences.en: Can you picture that threat?
sentences.zh: 你能想象那种威胁吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: Yes.

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: Okay.

sentences.en: Now picture what you'd like that place to look like 40 to 50 years from now.
sentences.zh: 现在想象一下，40到50年后的那个地方会是什么样子。

sentences.en: Not what you think it will look like, but what you'd like it to look like.
sentences.zh: 不是你认为它会是什么样子，而是你希望它是什么样子。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: Okay.

sentences.en: You have that picture in mind?
sentences.zh: 你脑海中有那个画面了吗？

sentences.en: And fourth and final question for the bonus round.
sentences.zh: 第四个也是最后一个加分轮的问题。

sentences.en: Picture something you can do today to work towards that vision that you have for
sentences.zh: 想象一件你今天就能做的事情，以便为实现你对40到50年后的那个愿景而努力。

sentences.en: 40 to 50 years from now.
sentences.zh: 40到50年后的样子。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: Okay.

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: Yeah.

sentences.en: Can you picture something?
sentences.zh: 你能想象出什么吗？

sentences.en: A little bit.
sentences.zh: 有一点。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: Okay.

sentences.en: So I'd have to think about it.
sentences.zh: 所以我得考虑一下。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: A little bit longer, but it gets you thinking, right?
sentences.zh: 时间稍微长了一点，但这确实让你开始思考，对吧？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: Exactly.

sentences.en: So this is the first step of a three-step process that we've developed.
sentences.zh: 这是我们开发的三步法中的第一步。

sentences.en: Those four questions I've done with hundreds of people now.
sentences.zh: 这四个问题我已经和几百人探讨过了。

sentences.en: Everybody can do the first three.
sentences.zh: 每个人都可以完成前三个问题。

sentences.en: Regardless of political stripe, regardless of viewpoints on a variety of other issues, everybody has a place in the world they care about.
sentences.zh: 不论政治倾向如何，不论对各种其他问题的观点如何，世界上每个人都有一个他们在乎的地方。

sentences.en: And everybody knows what the threat is to that place.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道那个地方面临着什么威胁。

sentences.en: And by the way, I've just made it personal for you.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我刚刚把它和你个人联系起来了。

sentences.en: And in 40 to 50 year timeframe, I've made it short for you.
sentences.zh: 在40到50年的时间范围内，我把它变得很短。

sentences.en: So you're thinking back to the National Academy of
sentences.zh: 所以你会回想起国家科学院的

sentences.en: Sciences and you're already thinking short and social.
sentences.zh: 观点，并且已经在思考简短和社交化了。

sentences.en: But now the fourth question is the stumper.
sentences.zh: 但现在第四个问题是难题。

sentences.en: What can you do to work towards that vision?
sentences.zh: 你能做些什么来朝着那个愿景努力？

sentences.en: And I would say 85 to 90% of people are stumped with that question.
sentences.zh: 我想85%到90%的人都会被这个问题难住。

sentences.en: They don't know what to do.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道该做什么。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: Yeah.

sentences.en: Now, as a clinical psychologist, if I just left you anxious, it's pretty good for business, but it's not very good for climate action.
sentences.zh: 作为一名临床心理学家，如果我只留给你焦虑，这对我的生意来说挺好，但对气候行动来说可不太好。

sentences.en: And that's where the second step comes in.
sentences.zh: 这就是第二步发挥作用的地方。

sentences.en: We've developed a set of procedures, a card sorting task, which is kind of fun, that helps people figure out first, what are they already doing on climate?
sentences.zh: 我们开发了一套程序，即卡片分类任务（挺好玩的），它首先帮助人们弄清楚：他们在气候方面已经在做什么？

sentences.en: And second, what's their next step on their own climate journey?
sentences.zh: 其次，他们在自己的气候征程上的下一步是什么？

sentences.en: And when we work that through with people, when we take them through that card sorting task, we find a couple of things happen.
sentences.zh: 当我们与人们一起完成这项工作，带他们经历卡片分类任务时，我们发现会发生几件事。

sentences.en: They really enjoy doing it.
sentences.zh: 他们真的很享受这个过程。

sentences.en: And as one 73-year-old said to me recently, I was delighted to see how much I'm already doing, but I was even more delighted to figure out what my next step was.
sentences.zh: 正如一位73岁的老人最近对我说的那样：“我很高兴看到自己已经在做这么多事情，但我更高兴的是弄清楚了我的下一步是什么。”

sentences.en: And then the third part of our process is what we call a climate commitment.
sentences.zh: 然后我们流程的第三部分是我们所说的“气候承诺”。

sentences.en: It's a psychology, behavioral economics, straight engagement contract where we get people to say, okay, here's my next step.
sentences.zh: 这是一个运用了心理学、行为经济学原理的直接参与契约，我们让人们说：“好吧，这是我的下一步。”

sentences.en: So who am I going to share that goal with?
sentences.zh: “那么我要和谁分享这个目标呢？”

sentences.en: And when am I going to do it?
sentences.zh: “我什么时候去做？”

sentences.en: What's the time frame?
sentences.zh: “时间框架是什么？”

sentences.en: And then the last part, which is kind of fun, is we ask people to picture a person or an organization whose values, visions, and goals they do not agree with, they disagree with,
sentences.zh: 然后最后一部分（挺有意思的），我们要求人们想象一个人或一个组织，他们的价值观、愿景和目标是他们所不同意的、他们所反对的，

sentences.en: and then make a commitment of a certain dollar amount that they will pledge to that person or organization if they don't carry through on the goal that they've just set.
sentences.zh: 然后许诺一笔特定金额的捐款，如果他们没有兑现刚刚设定的目标，就会把这笔钱捐给那个人或那个组织。

sentences.en: And usually when I ask them to identify an organization or person they don't agree with, there's nervous laughter in the room.
sentences.zh: 通常当我让他们说出一个他们不同意的组织或个人时，房间里会响起紧张的笑话声。

sentences.en: I'll give you one quick example, then I'll stop.
sentences.zh: 我举一个简单的例子，然后就不多说了。

sentences.en: I was doing this exercise at a retirement community in State College, Pennsylvania, which football fans would know is the home of Penn State.
sentences.zh: 当时我正在宾夕法尼亚州州立大学的一个退休社区做这个练习，美式橄榄球球迷会知道那是宾夕法尼亚州立大学（Penn State）所在地。

sentences.en: And when we got to the climate commitment part, I asked people to identify an organization or individual whose goals they didn't agree with.
sentences.zh: 当我们进入气候承诺部分时，我要求大家指出一个其目标他们不赞同的组织或个人。

sentences.en: And somebody wrote down Ohio State University.
sentences.zh: 有人写下了俄亥俄州立大学。

sentences.en: So now, from the outside, I could not have predicted that Ohio State would be a motivator for an older adult on climate change.
sentences.zh: 所以从外表来看，我本不可能预测到俄亥俄州立大学会成为老年人应对气候变化的动力。

sentences.en: But that person has told me what will motivate them.
sentences.zh: 但那个人告诉我什么会激励他们。

sentences.en: And it turns out that this combination of the first four questions I asked you, the card sort and the climate contract, is very effective in moving
sentences.zh: 事实证明，我向你提出的前四个问题的组合、卡片分类和气候契约，在推动人们从对气候变化的焦虑走向行动，

sentences.en: people from anxiety to action to habit on climate change.
sentences.zh: 再走向习惯方面非常有效。

sentences.en: Finally, I want to talk about something that isn't often brought up in conversations about climate change.
sentences.zh: 最后，我想谈谈一个在气候变化对话中不常被提起的话题。

sentences.en: And this is the physical and mental consequences of climate change.
sentences.zh: 这就是气候变化带来的生理和心理后果。

sentences.en: Earlier this year, the APA issued a report with EcoAmerica outlining the potential impact of climate change on mental health.
sentences.zh: 今年早些时候，美国心理学协会（APA）与EcoAmerica发布了一份报告，概述了气候变化对心理健康的潜在影响。

sentences.en: Are older adults more vulnerable to these changes?
sentences.zh: 老年人对这些变化是否更脆弱？

sentences.en: Is that something that you've looked at and studied?
sentences.zh: 这是你关注和研究过的事情吗？

sentences.en: Well, that's a very good point, Audrey.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个很好的观点，奥黛丽。

sentences.en: Older adults are more vulnerable to a variety of effects of both physical and mental health effects of climate change.
sentences.zh: 老年人对气候变化的各种生理和心理健康影响更为脆弱。

sentences.en: In fact, there have been a number of studies, including the most recent study by EcoAmerica and American Psychological Association,
sentences.zh: 事实上，已经有很多研究，包括EcoAmerica和美国心理学协会最近的研究，

sentences.en: that highlight the special vulnerabilities of older adults.
sentences.zh: 都强调了老年人特殊的脆弱性。

sentences.en: The way that I think about this is following the lead of the Department of Defense.
sentences.zh: 我对这件事的思考方式是效仿国防部的做法。

sentences.en: The Department of Defense says that climate change is a threat multiplier, a strategic threat multiplier.
sentences.zh: 国防部表示，气候变化是一个威胁倍增器，一个战略威胁倍增器。

sentences.en: And I think when you look at older people, they are particularly vulnerable because they are more likely to have chronic health conditions.
sentences.zh: 我认为当你审视老年人时，他们格外脆弱，因为他们更有可能患有慢性健康状况。

sentences.en: Although the rates of mental illness are lower in later life than in other parts of the
sentences.zh: 尽管晚年精神疾病的发病率低于生命的其他阶段，但一旦发生，

sentences.en: lifespan, when they occur, they're likely to be as difficult and a challenge to respond to as at other parts of the lifespan.
sentences.zh: 它们可能和生命其他阶段一样难以应对且充满挑战。

sentences.en: So older adults are vulnerable in many of the same ways and have some additional
sentences.zh: 因此，老年人在许多方面具有相同的脆弱性，并且还有一些额外的

sentences.en: physical vulnerabilities like a lessened ability to deal with heat stress, for example, and thermoregulation in a heat wave and that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 生理脆弱性，例如应对热应激的能力下降，例如在热浪中的体温调节能力等等。

sentences.en: What Gray and Green is trying to do, however, is to say, yes, the threats are real and older adults are vulnerable, but older adults are not only victims of climate change,
sentences.zh: 然而，Gray 和 Green 想要表达的是，没错，这些威胁是真实存在的，老年人也确实很脆弱，但老年人不仅仅是气候变化的受害者，

sentences.en: but potential leaders of climate action.
sentences.zh: 更是气候行动的潜在领导者。

sentences.en: So both are true.
sentences.zh: 所以这两点都是事实。

sentences.en: The one thing I would point out is that the recent report by EcoAmerica and APA, which Susan Clayton and Christy Manning chaired from the APA, continues APA's work in this area.
sentences.zh: 我要指出的第一点是，EcoAmerica 和 APA 最近发布的报告——该报告由 APA 的苏珊·克莱顿和克里斯蒂·曼宁主持——延续了 APA 在这一领域的工作。

sentences.en: Janet Swim and her colleagues published an earlier report.
sentences.zh: 珍妮特·斯威姆和她的同事们此前曾发表过一份报告。

sentences.en: And one of the key themes there is building resilience, both at the individual and community level.
sentences.zh: 其中的一个核心主题是增强韧性，包括个人层面和社区层面。

sentences.en: And in many ways, that's what Gray and Green is about, trying to help individuals become more
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，这就是 Gray 和 Green 的宗旨，它试图帮助个人变得更有

sentences.en: resilient and through older people and their circles of influence, helping communities become more resilient in the face of climate change.
sentences.zh: 韧性，并通过老年人及其影响力圈子，帮助社区在面对气候变化时变得更有韧性。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Smeyer, thank you so much for joining us.
sentences.zh: 好的，斯迈尔博士，非常感谢您做客我们的节目。

sentences.en: It's been a real pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这真是一段非常愉快的时光。

sentences.en: Thanks, Audrey.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，奥黛丽。

sentences.en: I've enjoyed it.
sentences.zh: 我度过了一段愉快的时光。

sentences.en: Thanks for listening to our podcaSt. Make sure you check out our other episodes of Speaking of Psychology, and please subscribe if you haven't already.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听我们的播客。请务必查看我们的《心理学谈话》其他期节目，如果你还没订阅，请点击订阅。

sentences.en: We are a proud member of the APA Podcast Network, which includes other great podcasts.
sentences.zh: 我们是美国心理学协会播客网络的自豪成员，该网络还包含其他优秀的播客。

sentences.en: Please check out APA Journal's Dialogue if you want to hear about the latest and most exciting psychology research.
sentences.zh: 如果你想了解最新、最令人兴奋的心理学研究，请查看《APA期刊对话》。

sentences.en: And if you're interested in the practice of psychology, you can listen to Progress Notes.
sentences.zh: 如果你对心理学实践感兴趣，可以收听《进展纪要》。

sentences.en: Topics include how healthcare policy and social media affect practicing psychologists.
sentences.zh: 话题包括医疗政策和社交媒体如何影响执业心理学家。

sentences.en: You can find those podcasts on iTunes, Stitcher, or wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 你可以在iTunes、Stitcher或任何你获取播客的地方找到这些播客。

sentences.en: You can also go to our website, speakingofpsychology.org, to listen to even more episodes and gather more resources on the topics we discussed.
sentences.zh: 你也可以访问我们的网站speakingofpsychology.org，收听更多期节目并收集有关我们讨论话题的更多资源。

sentences.en: Thanks for joining us.
sentences.zh: 感谢您的加入。

sentences.en: I'm Audrey Hamilton with the American Psychological Association, and this is Speaking of Psychology.
sentences.zh: 我是美国心理学协会的奥黛丽·汉密尔顿，这里是《心理学谈话》。
